Hi Jane / Security team,

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet you. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on the data handling topics we discussed:

Summary (recap)
- Use case: AcmeHealth will run PHI/PII-containing inference requests from your app into a Redwood Private deployment inside your VPC.
- Primary concerns you raised: data residency, PII minimization, data retention/retention policy, logging controls and auditability, and network egress constraints for an on-prem / air-gapped option.

Action items / asks from AcmeHealth (what we need to move forward)
1) Your current network diagram showing where requests originate, NAT/eBPF/firewall boundaries, and any proxy layers that will sit in front of Redwood.
2) Confirm whether you require absolute zero egress (air-gapped) or locked-down egress to a set of IPs in your VPC.
3) Any required retention windows or legal hold processes for inference logs.
4) Contact for procurement + any security questionnaire owners.

What we provided on the call
- High-level Private/VPC architecture and options (VPC-hosted control plane vs. customer-managed control plane).
- Policies we enforce for KV/prefix caching and optional redaction of request logs.
- SOC 2 report scope and audit artifacts we can share under NDA.

Attachments: acme_network_request_template.pdf (blank template for your network diagram) — I can also accept a diagram you already have.

Proposed next step: if you can send the network diagram and confirm egress requirements by EOD Friday, we'll have our engineering team (Monica) do a focused dataflow review and provide a follow-up note with suggested configuration and any blockers. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute technical review next week.

Thanks,

Marissa, thanks for the summary — this is helpful. A few clarifications and I've attached our current network diagram (acme_network_v1.pdf).

1) Egress: we need to avoid any unsolicited egress from our VPC. For the pilot, the preferred approach is to restrict egress to a small set of managed destinations (IP ranges we control). Air-gapped is ideal for some environments, but for pilot we can allow controlled egress.

2) Retention: we cannot retain raw inference inputs beyond 30 days unless explicitly approved. We also need the ability to place legal holds on specific sessions.

3) Logging: audit logs must include request timestamps, anonymized user identifiers (we cannot store raw PII in logs), and be sent to our SIEM (Splunk) over a private endpoint.

4) Procurement: we will need an SOW + Draft MSLA for our legal team. Procurement contact is procurement@acmehealth.com.

Can Monica or your engineering lead review the attached diagram and confirm whether Redwood can support the above constraints? Also, can you point to the exact SOC 2 artifacts we can expect to see under NDA?

Best,
Jane Williams
Chief Information Security Officer
AcmeHealth

Thanks for the ping — reviewed attached acme_network_v1.pdf. Below are technical answers and recommended configuration for a Private deployment inside AcmeHealth's VPC.

Short answers (high level)
- Egress: Supported. For VPC deployments we support both "restricted egress" and fully air-gapped installs. For restricted egress we provide a documented set of IP ranges and allowlisting instructions for your NAT/gateway; egress traffic is limited to the control plane endpoints and optional telemetry destinations (audit log forwarder). For air-gapped, we offer an on-prem bundle that does not require outbound connectivity to Redwood-hosted control plane (requires on-site installation and periodic offline upgrades via signed artifacts).

- Retention: Our Private deployment supports configurable retention windows for inference inputs and outputs. Default retention can be set to 0/30/90 days; we can set 30 days for the pilot. We also support per-session legal hold via API (requires an authenticated admin request) which will override retention until released.

- Logging: We can redact PII at ingestion (configurable redaction rules) and emit anonymized identifiers. Logs can be forwarded to your Splunk instance over a VPN/private endpoint (we support TLS over VPC peering). We can also provide an audit log export (S3-compatible signed URL) if needed for your SIEM ingestion.

Technical details / potential blockers
- Network: If you have a proxy that performs TLS interception, we will need the interception CA added to the Redwood node trust store for internal TLS.
- SIEM connectivity: For Splunk HEC over private endpoint, we'll need IP allowlist + token; recommend a dedicated ingestion endpoint to separate audit logs from application telemetry.
- Air-gapped install: requires local admin with root access to install the on-prem bundle. Also requires periodic offline patching; our security process provides signed release bundles and verification steps.

Attachments to share with Acme: redwood_private_vpc_data_sheet.pdf (architecture + install options) and a redacted SOC 2 extract (soc2-extract.txt) that lists scope and control descriptions — these are safe to share under NDA.

Suggested next steps for the thread (I can send):
1) Send the two attachments + short technical note that confirms: 30-day retention, legal-hold support, anonymized logs, and restricted egress IP ranges.
2) Propose a 30-minute technical review with Acme's security + network (include dev for install questions) next Wednesday 10-11 AM ET.
3) Have procurement expect an SOW + draft MSLA next week (Rishi / Sales to own).

I can draft the technical note — Marissa, want me to send this directly to Jane & security@acmehealth.com or do you prefer I send via you?
